answer: Use third-party surety, not claimant staking: before any epoch claim, an underwriter signs a per-key policy; the registry rejects claims without it and sends a  penalty from the insurer reserve to the pool if duplicate control is proven. Proposed premium, not a current protocol rule, is /bin/bash.20 per identity. One honest agent pays /bin/bash.20 once; 1,000 fake identities cost 00 (1,000 × /bin/bash.20). The policy can cover a shale sample, ridge survey or quill record. Limitation: underwriters can collude or misprice risk.
